The proposed solution uses the integral relationship:
$$
\int_{a}^{b} f(x) \, dx + \int_{f(a)}^{f(b)} f^{-1}(y) \, dy = b f(b) - a f(a)
$$
We established the limits and computed the boundary values correctly: $a=-9$, $b=11$, $f(a)=-4$, $f(b)=14$.
The right-hand side is $11(14) - (-9)(-4) = 154 - 36 = 118$.
So, $\int_{-9}^{11} f(x) \, dx + \int_{-4}^{14} f^{-1}(y) \, dy = 118$.

We need to compute $J = \int_{-4}^{14} f^{-1}(y) \, dy$.
Using the substitution $u = (y-5)/9$, we found:
$$
J = 9 \int_{-1}^{1} (u^7 + 6u^5 + 3u^3 + 1) \, du
$$
Since $u^7, u^5, u^3$ are odd functions, their integral over $[-1, 1]$ is zero.
$$
J = 9 \left( 0 + 0 + 0 + \int_{-1}^{1} 1 \, du \right) = 9 (2) = 18
$$
The proposed solution correctly derived the setup for this integral but then incorrectly calculated its value, stating $51.75$ instead of $18$.

Using the correct value $J=18$:
$$
\int_{-9}^{11} f(x) \, dx = 118 - 18 = 100
$$
Since the proposed final answer was $66.25$ (based on the incorrect calculation $J=51.75$), the final answer is not correct.
